chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus: In

a man who had several slaves said to them, 'Whichever of you taught me a verse from the Book of Allah, he is free.' One of them taught him, and then the master died, and it was not known which of them had taught him. It is said that he is selected by lot. He said, 'And it is not permissible for anyone to select him except the Imam, because he has a specific recitation and supplication for the lot that no one else knows.'
ai.seo_question: How is a specific slave chosen for manumission when the master's condition is ambiguous and he has died?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the procedure for manumission when the specific slave who fulfilled the condition of teaching a Quranic verse is unknown among several candidates. It highlights the Imam's exclusive authority in drawing lots (*qur'ah*), as he alone possesses the requisite knowledge of the specific supplications and recitations associated with the act, ensuring the legal validity of the emancipation.
